trials.claim: Lifetime access to Insecure Web on Plan 1
trials.claimQuote:
Lifetime access to Insecure Web
- You must redeem your code(s) within 60 days of purchase
trials.reasoning: A reviewer reports using the lifetime deal for years and calls it the best LTD, supporting lifetime access. The other reviews only describe temporary approval or setup delays, not loss of lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: Unfortunately, I don’t have access to the full functionality until this is sorted out.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports not receiving full functionality after purchase, undermining lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: It’s been a week since I made the purchase, and my company still hasn’t been approved
exhibits.argument: Access was still blocked a week after purchase pending approval, undermining immediate lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: This is hands down the best Ltd on here. I’ve used it for years.
exhibits.argument: The reviewer confirms long-term use of the lifetime deal and calls it the best LTD.

trials.claim: Unlimited threat intelligence research and feed download
trials.claimQuote:
Unlimited threat intelligence research
- Unlimited threat intelligence feed download
trials.reasoning: Reviewers report credits being consumed quickly and several extra payments being charged, which materially limits the promised unlimited research and feed download.

exhibits.quote: I added 5 domains and didn’t realize how quickly my credits would be consumed.
exhibits.argument: Credits are consumed quickly, contradicting unlimited research and feed download.

exhibits.quote: After a few weeks, I logged in and noticed that several payments had been charged to my credit card.
exhibits.argument: Extra payments were charged for usage, contradicting unlimited included use.

trials.claimQuote:
Stack up to 3 codes
- 50 credits per month
- Up to 4 company impersonation domains
trials.reasoning: The exhibits show extra charges and confusion about pricing, but neither states how many credits were actually received, so they do not prove or disprove 50 credits per month.

exhibits.quote: To be safe, I removed the card, and that immediately triggered an invoice of over $180.
exhibits.argument: 50 monthly credits were insufficient and led to a large extra invoice.

exhibits.quote: After entering the domain information, it shows a price. It is unclear to me if that affects me?
exhibits.argument: User sees an extra price when adding domains, undermining that credits cover usage.

trials.claim: Up to 4 company impersonation domains and 4 threat intelligence entities on Plan 1
trials.claimQuote:
Up to 4 company impersonation domains
- Monitor up to 4 threat intelligence entities
trials.reasoning: One confused reviewer about 'organisations' does not clearly show the product's domain or entity limit, so it is too weak to prove or disprove the up-to-4 limit.

exhibits.quote: When I enter two organisations (thought this might be something like areas to organise domains), I can not access the first one after entering the second.
exhibits.argument: Buyer could not use even two organisations at once, undermining up to 4 domains/entities.

trials.claim: All future Pay as you go Plan updates included
trials.claimQuote: All future Pay as you go Plan updates
trials.reasoning: The same quote only says one coming feature will be available for credits; it does not establish that all future Pay as you go Plan updates are included.

exhibits.quote: In the QA they mentioned penetration tests are coming and will be included for credits.
exhibits.argument: Coming updates will cost extra credits rather than being included.

exhibits.quote: In the QA they mentioned penetration tests are coming and will be included for credits.
exhibits.argument: The reviewer confirms upcoming features will be included for existing credit holders.

trials.reasoning: The review confirms a refund was issued, but it does not mention the 60-day period, so it does not verify the specific 60-day guarantee.

exhibits.quote: Their support was professional, understanding, and they even issued me a refund
exhibits.argument: The reviewer confirms the vendor actually issued a refund as promised.
